Travel back in time to an age before digital, before PCs, smartphones, satellites and throw-away culture. In that era a wristwatch was something you kept for life, something to be treasured and passed from one generation to the next. The mechanical watch movements of the 1960s and 1970s represent the culmination of hundreds of years of technological development. With the advent of quartz watches in the late 1970s this technology became obsolete. The great thing about a watch that works with obsolete technology is: you don't have to worry about it becoming obsolete! What is a 5 year-old smartphone worth today? Nothing. What will the latest smartwatch be worth in 5 years time? Nothing. And not just in monetary value. Please call 01572 827787 or email: uppinghamfootclinic@gmail.com for more information. ​ My name is Jo Barker, the proud owner of Uppingham Foot Clinic in Rutland. I qualified as a Podiatrist in 2002, with a First Class Honours Degree in Podiatry, from Durham School of Podiatry (University of Sunderland). I started my career as an NHS Podiatrist at Rutland Memorial Hospital, working as a Specialist Podiatrist in Biomechanics. My interest in lower limb biomechanics,and musculo-skeletal disorders, has continued throughout my career, and I have continued to develop this as a specialism. In January 2014, I started my own private practice based in Uppingham. This allowed me to continue working as a Podiatrist, a job which I am devoted to, whilst also being able to be a flexible working mum to three children! In 2018 I had three clinics in Uppingham, at the Surgery, Uppingham School Sports Centre and Victoria Pharmacy. In January 2019 we launched Uppingham Foot Clinic in our own premises in Bear Yard, with ongoing renovation we are transforming the building to create our brand new 'home'! I am passionate about all aspects of foot health and foot care, and the important role it has to play in our general health and well being. Whether it was building elaborate LEGO sets with my family or forging new connections with friends, I found joy in creating and sharing. My love for baking began in my childhood, baking Christmas cookies with my maw maw and nana and making weekly treats with my mom. I didn't realize it at the time, but I was falling in love with the way food, especially my nana’s poundcake, brought our family together. Every year, whether it was a holiday or a family reunion, people lined up just to get a slice of her cakes. I saw how food could create joy and connection, and that realization sparked a deeper passion in me. When I was 11, I attempted to make cheesecake for family and friends. Though I failed miserably, that failure ignited a drive within me. Today, at 22, I’m proud to run Burton’s Bakery, where I can share my passion and bring smiles to customers' faces, one slice and one cake at a time! Whether through photos on Instagram, TikTok videos, or face-to-face interactions, sharing this journey and making people happy has always been my dream. My ultimate goal is to expand Burton’s Bakery into its own space and grow the franchise even further. Thank you for being a part of my journey. Book a Table Explore Menu A Historic Gem in the Heart of Pluckley The Black Horse Restaurant is nestled in the charming village of Pluckley, known for its rich history and picturesque scenery. Dating back to the 15th century, our building has witnessed centuries of change while maintaining its traditional character, from its beamed ceilings to its inviting inglenook fireplaces. Pluckley itself has a fascinating past, once known as “Pluchelei” in the Domesday Book. The area thrived in the 13th century with weaving and milling industries, utilising water-powered mills to process local wool. Later, Pluckley became famous for its brickworks, producing the distinctive “blue” bricks used in historic buildings such as Pluckley Church. Legends even speak of ghostly apparitions wandering the old churchyard, adding to Pluckley’s reputation as one of England’s most haunted villages. Find us on Facebook OUR MENUS BOOK TABLE About Us Water Street means a lot to us. Five out of the six of us went to Water Street Primary School, so this really does feel like coming home. We’re Skipton born and bred, and after years of dreaming about opening a restaurant in our hometown, Drift is our next big step. Fourteen years ago, we took a leap of faith and took over The White Horse Inn in Thornton, and we’re proud to say we’re still there today. You can find us at The White Horse Inn, Well Heads, Thornton, BD13 3SJ, or call 01274 834268 . After the success of The White Horse, we’ve always wanted to create something closer to home. Somewhere relaxed, welcoming and full of the kind of food we love to eat ourselves. People often ask what style of food we cook, but we’ve never liked being boxed in. Our menu will be guided by good ingredients, proper cooking and dishes that simply taste great. If we’re proud to eat it ourselves, you’ll find it at Drift. We’re dedicated to creating a warm, friendly atmosphere with excellent food, genuine hospitality and great service. We can’t wait to welcome you through the doors.
